introH2: 🏖️ What types of White Sand Beach hotels are there on Koh Chang, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: White Sand Beach (Hat Sai Khao) is the longest, liveliest beach on Koh Chang and the one with the most to eat and do — it's the first beach the road passes after you come off the ferry, and the spot most travelers picture when they think of Koh Chang. But "a White Sand Beach hotel" doesn't come in just one shape, and that's what makes choosing more fun than you'd expect — some are 4-star family resorts with lots of pools, including a rooftop infinity pool with sea views; some are wooden bungalows right on a quiet stretch at the far end where you open your door onto the sand; and some are budget stays in the middle of the action, within walking distance of restaurants, bars, and the sea. Plenty of people pay up and end up with a location or vibe that doesn't match their trip, then feel it wasn't worth it. This article rounds up 9 stays on White Sand Beach that we've reviewed in depth — from the northern end through the middle of the beach to the southern end. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms, with the upsides and the honest caveats laid out, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links included.
mrtHtml: Koh Chang has no train. Getting there means taking a car ferry across from the mainland piers in Trat province (Centerpoint Pier or Ao Thammachat Pier) over to the island, which takes about 30–45 minutes, then a songthaew (shared red truck) on to White Sand Beach, another 10–20 minutes — White Sand Beach is on the north of the island and the closest to the piers. On the island, the main way to get around is the red songthaews that run along the main road, or renting a motorbike to explore on your own (the road has some steep, winding hills, so take care). What's worth understanding about location within White Sand Beach: the northern end has a wide beach and shallow water and is quieter than mid-beach; the middle of the beach is the liveliest, within walking distance of all the restaurants, bars, and the night market; the southern end and the inland side are quieter and cheaper, but some places mean walking down a hill or taking a roundabout route to the beach. In high season (Nov–Apr) the sea is clear and calm and best for swimming, while in the rainy season (May–Oct) prices drop a lot but the surf is rougher and the water murkier.

entries.storyHtml: If we're starting with the "most complete" option on White Sand Beach, plenty of reviewers point to KC Grande Resort & Spa — a large 4-star beachfront resort that landed a great corner spot at the northern end of the beach. Step out of your room and you're on soft sand with shallow water, yet it's far enough from the mid-beach bar strip that nights don't get too loud. The thing people talk about most, and the real star here, is the pools — the resort has 4 in total, the highlight being a roughly 40-meter infinity-edge pool on the rooftop with a Horizon Pool Bar looking out over a wide stretch of the Koh Chang sea. Plenty agree that sunset up here is the best-value time of day. There's also a swim-up pool bar by the beach and a cave-style pool with a slide that kids love, plus a kids' club, a spa, and a beachfront breakfast buffet that reviews praise for its variety. The important thing to understand before booking is that the resort is split into two zones divided by a road — the Seaside zone is right on the sand, walk straight down to the beach, ideal for families with young kids, while the Hillside zone on the hill side has newer rooms and jacuzzis but you cross the road to reach the beach. Honest caveats from the reviews: White Sand Beach is busy at peak times, and the beach bars have live music some nights that carries to the closer rooms; some older beachfront rooms look more dated than the newer Hillside ones; and prices run high by Koh Chang standards. If you're coming as a family or mainly to swim and want a resort that has everything in one place so you never need to leave, KC Grande is the most well-rounded choice, and it's been a top name on White Sand Beach for years.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Get up to the rooftop infinity pool and Horizon Bar at least once at sunset. If you book the Seaside side, ask for a room away from the beach bar to avoid the music at night. For newer rooms with a jacuzzi, choose Hillside (Ocean View) and accept crossing the road to the beach.

entries.name: Kacha Resort & Spa, Koh Chang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Middle of White Sand Beach · walk along the beach to everything
entries.addr: 88-89 Moo 4, White Sand Beach, Koh Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among the White Sand Beach stays we've reviewed, if you go by score, Kacha Resort & Spa is the highest-scoring in this article at 9.3 from 174 reviews on Trip.com. The number-one selling point is the location — the resort sits right in the middle of White Sand Beach. Unlike the places at the head or far end of the beach, being in the center means you can walk along the shore in either direction, and the seafront restaurants, bars, massage shops, convenience stores, and night market are all just a few minutes' walk away — so much so that plenty of reviews say they "never needed to call a ride the whole trip." It's a large family resort with 206 rooms in 12 types, straddling the road as a Seaside zone on the sand and a Hillside zone on the hill side. The highlight for families is 2 pools with a separate kids' pool and a slide, with swim-up bars at both pools, plus a beach out front with shallow water that's safe for young kids, and a breakfast buffet with sea views that reviews praise often. Honest caveats to know: the resort has been open around 20 years, so room standards aren't consistent across every building — the Hillside zone has been renovated more recently and the rooms feel fresher, while some rooms in the older zone are starting to show their age. On top of that, food at the resort is fairly pricey, poolside chairs run short at peak times, and the water out front is so shallow you have to walk far before you can swim. Best suited to families and couples who want a beachfront stay in the middle of the convenience at a reachable price — just ask for a renovated room when you book.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: State clearly when booking that you want a recently renovated room, and pick the Hillside zone if you're after fresher rooms. Go down to claim a poolside chair early in high season because it gets crowded. Have breakfast at the resort, then walk out for seafood at the beachfront restaurants just a few minutes away — better value.
pros: Highest score in the article at 9.3 · mid-beach location, walk to everything
2 pools with a kids' pool and slide + shallow, safe beach for kids

entries.storyHtml: If you want to wake up and step straight onto the beach without paying luxury-resort prices, Koh Chang Grandview Resort is the one real reviews talk about most for "location and seafront atmosphere." This 3-star resort sits on a wide plot of land right in the middle of White Sand Beach — a few steps and you're on the sand, while across the road there are convenience stores, restaurants, and shops easily within walking distance. Plenty of reviews say "staying here, you barely need to rent a vehicle." After location, the thing that comes up most is the outdoor saltwater pool in the seafront garden, set in a chill, photogenic corner, especially around sunset, plus a large shady garden where kids can run around and a beach bar where you can sit with a drink and the view. The honest part, straight from the reviews, is that room quality isn't consistent across every building — some rooms are renovated, clean and comfortable, while some older bungalows are still run-down with age, with complaints about dim bathroom lighting and worn details. The safe move is to pick a newer room type like the Duplex or Pool Side and add a note asking for a recently renovated room. Best suited to families, couples, and groups of friends set on swimming and walking around to eat and explore mid-beach, with expectations set mainly on "location and atmosphere."
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a newer room in the Duplex / Pool Side / Seaview group and add a note asking for a recently renovated room when you book. Chill by the saltwater pool or reserve a beach-bar table at sunset. Check the last ferry crossing and ask whether there's any construction during your stay.

entries.storyHtml: Banpu Koh Chang Resort is a long-standing wooden-bungalow resort that secured a spot right on the sand back before White Sand Beach filled up with places to stay, and there are two things to know before booking that bear directly on the decision. First: it now operates as adults only, so you can't book it coming as a family with young kids — but if you're a couple, a group of friends, or traveling solo and want a quiet seafront vibe without kids running around, this is the spot many choose over a large family resort. Second: the appeal here is the seafront location and the feel of bungalows in a green garden, planted long enough ago that the trees shade the whole grounds — not luxury. A few steps through the garden from your bungalow and you're on the sand, and a few minutes' walk gets you to restaurants, convenience stores, and the bar strip. The thing that earns better-than-expected praise is the seafront breakfast buffet, which reviews say has tastier Thai food than the price suggests, plus friendly staff. Honest caveats to know: the rooms split into two clear characters — some of the original wooden bungalows are old and dark versus the much brighter new-building rooms, a gap big enough to change the feel of the whole trip, so ask for a new-building room when you book. The pool is also fairly small for the size of the resort, the beach out front along this stretch is narrow with rocks underwater, and on some nights you can hear nearby shops and bars. Best suited to couples and adult travelers who value the seafront location and convenience over plush rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a new-building or renovated room when you book — don't leave it to chance, because the gap with the old wooden bungalows is huge. Don't miss the seafront breakfast; try going early before the crowd. If you want a wide stretch of sand to walk into the water easily, walk along the beach a bit further north.

entries.addr: 99/9 Moo 4, White Sand Beach, Koh Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: If you want a "good-looking pool with sea views at a reachable price" on White Sand Beach, Chang Buri Resort & Spa is a name many reviews choose — a 4-star resort set at the southern end of the beach, with around 110 rooms. What sets it apart is the way it splits across two zones on opposite sides of the road — a more affordable Hillside zone up on the hill, and a seafront zone with villas and rooms that have wider sea views. The most talked-about highlight is the infinity pool on the seafront side, its edge spilling out as if it joins the sea — a popular spot to take photos and chill, especially at sunset, and plenty of reviews say it's the main reason they chose to stay here. There's a separate kids' pool and the Apsara Spa for a relaxing massage, plus a far-end location where you walk out to restaurants, massage shops, and bars in a few minutes. The thing to understand before booking: the resort sits on a hill and rocks, with no direct path down to the sandy beach from the resort — you walk along an adjacent path down, about 5 minutes. On top of that, some Hillside-zone rooms are plainer and mean crossing the road to the seafront pool side, there's a bar at the entrance with music at night, and the Wi-Fi is unstable in some rooms. The straight advice from the reviews is that if your budget allows, go for a seafront-zone room — you get clearly better views, more space, and closer access to the pool than the Hillside side. Best suited to couples and families who want a good-looking pool near the food and drinks at a reachable price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget allows, go straight for a Seaside room or villa — you get the view, the space, and closeness to the infinity pool. Head up to the pool bar at the seafront pool at sunset. If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room deeper inside or on the side away from the road, and bring a mobile data SIM since the Wi-Fi is unstable in some rooms.

entries.storyHtml: If budget is the main brief and you want to stay mid White Sand Beach without overthinking it, Alina Grande Hotel & Resort is the one with the lowest starting price and the one reviews call the best value in this article, from around ฿900/night. It's a mid-range resort hotel in the heart of the White Sand Beach area, about 350 meters from the shore, or a 3–5 minute walk to the sea, and step out the door and you're among restaurants, convenience stores, massage shops, and bars lining the road — plenty of international reviews rate this location's "walkability" highly. The two things real reviews agree on are that the rooms are noticeably wider than the price suggests and that the pool in the garden is bigger and cleaner than you'd expect for a hotel at this level, with some even calling it a lap pool. The important thing to understand before booking is that the resort is split into two buildings on opposite sides of the road — the beach-side building is older but closer to the sea, and the road-side building is newer with nicer rooms. If newness matters to you, ask for the new road-side building when you book. Honest caveats: it's a mid-range resort with buildings that have aged, especially the beach side where some spots are still rough; the Wi-Fi is sometimes unstable; breakfast is fairly basic; there's no lift; and the lively White Sand Beach area has bar and motorbike noise in the evenings. Best suited to budget travelers, couples, and families who want to stay mid-beach without spending much, with expectations set on "value" rather than "luxury."
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for the new road-side building (main building) when you book if room newness matters. Request an inward-facing room that doesn't face the road, and bring earplugs if you're a light sleeper. There's no lift, so if you have heavy bags or are traveling with older guests, ask for a ground-floor room, and have a backup mobile data plan.

entries.storyHtml: If you want to stay on White Sand Beach on a budget but don't want to sleep right on the mid-beach road with noise all night, Paddy's Palms Resort is a choice real reviews talk about for being "quiet and friendly." It's a small resort of around 30 rooms tucked into a shady green garden in the far-end zone of White Sand Beach, open since 2006 under management with an Irish touch, as the name "Paddy's" suggests. The thing to understand before booking is that this isn't a beachfront resort — the resort is on the inland side of the road, about 1.3 kilometers from the shore, or roughly a 10-minute walk — and the upside of being inland is that it's quieter and more private than hotels right on the main road with bars that run late. The most talked-about highlight is the pool with a jacuzzi set in the green garden, a quiet, uncrowded atmosphere, plus the in-house Paddy's Palms Irish pub, which serves international food, has cold beer, and shows live sports in the evening — which many international reviews say makes it feel like home. Another thing that earns consistent praise is the breakfast, done better than you'd expect for a resort this size. Honest caveats: beyond not being beachfront, the buildings have been open since 2006, so some rooms are starting to show their age and some ground-floor rooms get little light, restaurant service is slow at times when it's busy, and reception often closes after about 10pm. Best suited to couples, travelers, and budget types who value cleanliness, quiet, and a chill evening atmosphere over a sea view from the room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Allow about 10 minutes to walk to the beach, or rent one of the resort's bikes / call a songthaew if it's hot. Ask for an upper-floor room with light and a garden view, and avoid ground-floor rooms near the pub if you're a light sleeper. Drop by the Irish pub for the football in the evening, and let them know your arrival time in advance since reception closes after 10pm.

entries.storyHtml: If your budget is genuinely tight but you still want an AC bungalow with a pool within walking distance of White Sand Beach, The White Elephant Resort is a choice where reviews say "good value" is the phrase that fits best. It's a budget bungalow resort set on the hill on the southern side of White Sand Beach, near the sports bar of the same name, run by the same owner as both the bar and the resort, open since around 2016. The thing to understand before booking: this isn't a beachfront resort — the resort sits deeper inland on a hill, and walking down the hill to White Sand Beach takes about 5–10 minutes (the way back is uphill), traded for the quiet and the lower price. The heart of the place is the outdoor saltwater pool with a pool bar that the bungalows ring around, both a way to cool off and a gathering spot for guests, and many rooms have a private balcony opening straight onto the pool view, while some Superior rooms have a small kitchenette good for longer stays. The advantage is being next to the owner's sports bar where guests get a discount, ideal for sports fans who like to watch the football in the evening. Honest caveats: it's a budget stay where the buildings and rooms are starting to show their age, some reviews say it could use an upgrade, and there are complaints about cleanliness in the details, like dust under the bed; on nights with a big sports match there can be late noise from the bar zone. The overall score sits in the middle at around 7.3, normal for a budget stay that's "good value but with room to improve." Best suited to budget travelers, couples, and longer-stay guests who aren't fussed about sleeping right on the beach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Be ready for the 5–10 minute walk down the hill to the beach (uphill on the way back); plan ahead if you have a lot of luggage. Ask for a room away from the pool bar and sports bar zone if you're a light sleeper, since big-match nights can get late noise. Check the room at check-in and ask to switch right away if something's not OK.

entries.addr: 1/1 Moo 3, northern end of White Sand Beach, Koh Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Closing out with a choice for people who care more about a "beachfront location and quiet" than how new the room is — White Sand Beach Resort is one of the early resorts to plant itself on this beach, so it landed a lovely seafront plot that's hard to find now. The resort is red-roofed wooden bungalows and family rooms spread under big trees at the far northern end of White Sand Beach, the quietest and most private zone, with fewer people than mid-beach where the bars and restaurants are. The clear strength is the genuine beachfront location — open your door and walk onto the sand in a few steps, with clear water and seafront sunset views you can watch from the room and the restaurant, while still being able to walk along the beach into the central zone with restaurants and bars in about 10–15 minutes. The seafront restaurant is a wooden terrace under coconut palms that reviews praise for its dinner atmosphere. There's no pool as a main selling point here, because the beach and the sea out front are a better natural "pool." Honest caveats to brace for: these are older bungalows with rooms and buildings that have aged and need renovating, cleanliness isn't consistent every time, and the resort entrance is a steep road down a hill, about 1–1.5 kilometers, that some vehicles don't want to drive down (the resort usually offers pickup from a nearby convenience store). Best suited to couples and families who want to wake up to the sea right outside the room, like the quiet, and can accept older rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specify when booking that you want a Beach Front Room closest to the sand, since some rooms sit deeper in the garden without a full sea view. If you're not driving yourself, ask in advance about pickup from a nearby convenience store, since the entry road is steep. Check whether breakfast is included or extra, and choose free cancellation during the monsoon.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking real prices and comparing the 3 sites before booking every time. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms — we didn't stay ourselves. Banpu Koh Chang Resort operates as adults only, so families with young kids can't book it. Koh Chang has no train; getting to the island means taking a ferry from the Trat-side piers, about 30–45 minutes, then a vehicle on to White Sand Beach, another 10–20 minutes. In high season (Nov–Apr) the sea is clear and calm and best for swimming, prices rise and the good rooms fill fast, so book ahead. In the rainy season (May–Oct) prices drop a lot but the surf is rougher and the water murkier, and at times the ferry crossings may be adjusted. Article by Thailandaddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers often ask about White Sand Beach hotels, Koh Chang

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best White Sand Beach hotel on Koh Chang?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. By review score, Kacha Resort & Spa tops the article at 9.3, with a mid-beach location. For pools and family activities, KC Grande Resort & Spa has 4 pools including a rooftop infinity pool. For an infinity pool with sea views on a budget, Chang Buri Resort & Spa starts at ฿1,100. For the best value, Alina Grande starts at ฿900. And to open your door onto a quiet stretch of sand, White Sand Beach Resort at the far northern end.

faq.q: ❓ How much do White Sand Beach hotels on Koh Chang cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start around ฿900–2,800 per night. On the budget side: Alina Grande from ฿900, The White Elephant from ฿1,000, White Sand Beach Resort from ฿1,020, and Chang Buri from ฿1,100 (Hillside zone). Mid-range: Paddy's Palms ฿1,750 and Koh Chang Grandview ฿1,800. The 4-star family resorts like KC Grande and Kacha start at ฿2,400, and Banpu (adults only) from ฿2,800. All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard rooms; in high season and on long weekends prices run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Who is White Sand Beach, Koh Chang for · which zone should you stay in?
faq.a: White Sand Beach is the longest and liveliest beach on the island, with the most restaurants, bars, and markets, ideal for anyone who wants both the beach and the convenience of walking to everything. The northern end (KC Grande, White Sand Beach Resort) is quieter, with a wide beach. The middle of the beach (Kacha, Koh Chang Grandview, Alina Grande) is the liveliest, walk to everything. The southern end and the inland side (Chang Buri, Banpu, Paddy's Palms, White Elephant) are quieter and cheaper, but some places mean walking down a hill or taking a roundabout route to the beach.

faq.q: ❓ Which White Sand Beach hotel on Koh Chang is good for families with kids?
faq.a: The strongest for families are KC Grande Resort & Spa (4 pools, kids' club, kids' pool with slide) and Kacha Resort & Spa (2 pools + slide, shallow safe beach for kids). On the budget side there's Koh Chang Grandview and Alina Grande, which have pools and spacious family rooms. Banpu Koh Chang Resort is adults only, so families with young kids can't book it.

faq.q: ❓ Which White Sand Beach hotels are "truly beachfront," with the sand right outside your door?
faq.a: The ones truly on the sand where you can walk straight down are White Sand Beach Resort (bungalows at the northern end, open your door to the sand), Banpu Koh Chang Resort (bungalows in a garden on the sand · adults only), and the Seaside zone of KC Grande. Meanwhile Chang Buri is up on a hill with no direct path down, about a 5-minute walk around; Alina Grande is a 3–5 minute walk to the sea; and Paddy's Palms / The White Elephant are a 5–10 minute walk to the beach — so if a sea view from the room is the heart of your trip, choose the truly beachfront group.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Chang · how far ahead should you book?
faq.a: Getting to Koh Chang means taking a ferry from the Trat-side piers (Centerpoint / Ao Thammachat), about 30–45 minutes, then a songthaew on to White Sand Beach, another 10–20 minutes (White Sand Beach is the closest to the piers). In high season (Nov–Apr) and on long weekends, book at least 1–2 weeks ahead because the good rooms, especially villas and beachfront rooms, fill fast. In the rainy season (May–Oct) prices drop a lot, but check the weather and the ferry timetable. Every platform offers free cancellation; we recommend locking in a rate that way if your plans aren't set, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
